title: Dynamic health-profile fingerprinting for per-tenant autoscale admission & multi-region evacuation
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Problem: During multi-region failovers and high tail latency events we observe abrupt autoscaler thrashing or whole-tenant evacuations caused by coarse health signals. Current readiness/liveness probes are global and treat all tenants the same; a noisy tenant can force wider degradation, leading to SLO violations for other tenants.
proposed_approach: Introduce a lightweight ‘health-profile fingerprint’ emitted by each node: a digest summarizing recent probe signal distributions (success rate, tail latency percentiles, synthetic probe outcomes) tagged with tenant-weighted request-shape indicators.
Use fingerprints to compute per-tenant admission scores for autoscaler and circuit breaker decisions rather than relying on raw node-level boolean readiness alone.

Implement a staged evacuation playbook: node-level mitigation (request shaping, token-aware shedding) -> tenant-scoped throttling -> regional reroute -> graceful evacuation with warmstart hints for KV caching.
Coordinate with autoscaler to allow ‘soft admission’ windows where capacity is provisioned conservatively using fingerprint confidence, preventing immediate scale-down/up oscillations.
Add lightweight privacy-preserving aggregation so fingerprints can be used for routing without exposing per-tenant PII or request payloads.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant admission score computed and exposed in control plane for 90% of production routes; score used by autoscaler to influence scale decisions.
During a simulated noisy-tenant storm in regional failover tests, non-noisy tenants maintain >=95% of baseline successful request rate and meet 95th percentile latency SLOs.
Autoscaler thrash incidents reduced by >=60% in chaos tests where synthetic probe flaps are introduced.
Playbook documented with runbooks and example CLI ops for on-call; at least one DR drill completed with SRE sign-off.
Telemetry dashboards added: fingerprint distribution, admission score histogram, tenant impact matrix, and rollback triggers.
work_log: 2026-03-10: Ticket created by Sofia Chen — initial problem writeup and scope.

2026-03-11: Architecture sync with SRE and Runtime teams. Decided on fingerprint shape and minimal fields to avoid PII. Recorded notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/SRE/Health+Fingerprint+Design.
2026-03-12: Prototype agent change landed in feature branch (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4821). Instrumentation emits 128-bit base64 digest and a small set of numeric buckets.
2026-03-13: Integration tests for admission score included in canary harness. Early results show reduced scale churn in local sim. Open items: eviction policy tuning and dashboard queries.
risks: Fingerprint dimensionality: too coarse -> ineffective; too fine -> noisy and costly to aggregate.
Privacy/regulatory: we must avoid exposing per-tenant content. Need legal review if additional metadata is used.
Operational complexity: introducing a new signal in autoscaler control loop risks subtle interactions and requires staged rollout strategy.
Rollback path: if admission scores misclassify tenants, need fast mitigation to avoid wide evacuation. Playbook must be tested.
mitigations: Start with conservative weights for admission score and a simulated-only mode for first 2 cycles.
Expose a ‘confidence’ metric; autoscaler ignores fingerprints with low confidence and falls back to existing rules.
Create fail-open and fail-closed configurations per environment and a kill-switch in the control plane for immediate rollback.
Automate DR drill to validate playbook within the sprint; require SRE sign-off before full rollout.
implementation_notes: Fingerprint fields: windowed success_rate (1/5/15m), p50/p95/p99 latency buckets, synthetic probe checksum, request-shape histogram (short/med/long), and token-weighted request count.
Transport: append fingerprint to existing heartbeat protobuf; keep size < 256 bytes to avoid control-plane blowup.
Aggregation: use approximate quantiles (t-digest) and binning with HLL for tenant counts to keep memory bounds.
Autoscaler hook: admission score computation lives in autoscaler scoring module; initial version only biases scale-down decisions (conservative).
open_decisions: Should admission score influence scale-up or only scale-down initially? Proposal: scale-down only for first 4 weeks.
Fingerprint retention length in control plane — 1h vs 6h. Default proposal: 1h with on-demand historical fetch for longer analysis.
Whether to include KV-cache warmstart hints in fingerprints or derive them from separate telemetry stream.
